andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh notifies rules for direct election of urban mayors and chairpersons
facts: G.O.Ms.No. 211, MA&UD Department, dated 5 September 2026, notified election rules for municipal corporation mayors and ward members.
Voters will directly elect municipal corporation mayors and municipality or nagar panchayat chairpersons; each directly elected office-holder has a five-year term.
Deputy mayors and vice-chairpersons will be elected indirectly by eligible elected and ex-officio members.
The State announced a 14-day exercise, 8–21 September, to identify SC, ST, BC and women voters in 59 Urban Local Bodies for reservation purposes.
The rules apply to Andhra Pradesh municipal corporations with immediate effect; this notification does not itself announce polling dates.
andhraPradesh.summary: Andhra Pradesh notified statutory rules for ordinary Urban Local Body elections, providing for direct election of mayors and chairpersons while retaining indirect election for deputy mayors and vice-chairpersons. A voter-identification exercise for reservation purposes was scheduled across 59 ULBs from 8 to 21 September.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: 74th Constitutional Amendment; Part IX-A of the Constitution; State Election Commission and urban local self-government.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish direct election of mayors/chairpersons from indirect election of deputy mayors/vice-chairpersons; Article 243K concerns the State Election Commission.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how electoral design, reservation preparation and State Election Commission oversight affect representation and accountability in urban local governance.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: rules apply to Andhra Pradesh ULBs and schedule voter identification across 59 state ULBs.

- **When:** **5 September 2026**

# 2. Election method and term
| Office | Election method | Term |
|---|---|---|
| **Municipal corporation mayors; municipality and nagar panchayat chairpersons** | **Directly elected by voters** | **Five years** |
| **Deputy mayors; vice-chairpersons** | **Indirectly elected by eligible elected and ex-officio members** | — |
- **Ward members:** Rules also notified for **municipal corporation ward members**

# 3. Reservation-related exercise
- **Exercise:** Identify **SC, ST, BC and women voters** for reservation purposes in **59 Urban Local Bodies**
- **Schedule:** **8–21 September 2026**; **14 days**

> Exam angle: Test the direct-versus-indirect election method for AP urban local body offices.

andhraPradesh.headline: Veligallu project water released into right canal amid scarcity in Annamayya district
facts: On 6 September, water was released into the Veligallu project’s right canal at Galiveedu mandal, Annamayya district.
The initial release was 120 cusecs; officials planned to reduce it to 80 cusecs after 15 days.
About 0.5 TMC was earmarked for use through the end of October; the administration planned to replenish a similar quantity through the Handri-Neeva project.
Officials set a 30% maximum for filling tanks and prioritised drinking water, livestock needs and groundwater recharge.
Farmers were advised not to rely on project water for water-intensive crops and to consider dryland crops amid rainfall concerns.
andhraPradesh.summary: Water was released into Veligallu’s right canal as the district managed limited supplies for essential needs. The announced release plan includes a reduction in discharge after 15 days and a 0.5-TMC allocation through October; the report also described a proposed Handri-Neeva replenishment plan.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: River-basin and irrigation management; drought mitigation; sustainable and dryland agriculture in Rayalaseema.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The Veligallu project release took place at Galiveedu mandal in Annamayya district; distinguish the current 120-cusec release from the planned 80-cusec rate after 15 days.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how transparent, needs-based irrigation scheduling and crop diversification can balance drinking-water security, livestock needs and farm livelihoods during water stress.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: Veligallu project, Galiveedu mandal and the water allocation are in Annamayya district, Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh announces fresh social-security pension application window
facts: The State announced that fresh applications for social-security pensions would be accepted from 7 to 16 September 2026.
Eligible people not currently receiving pension benefits may apply through Swarna Gramam and Swarna Ward centres across the State.
Applications are to be registered online and undergo e-KYC during the application period.
The reported schedule sets preliminary eligibility scrutiny for 17–21 September and physical and departmental verification for 22–24 September.
Applicants were asked to provide Aadhaar and a Rice Card or income certificate, plus relevant category-specific documents.
andhraPradesh.summary: Andhra Pradesh announced a new application window for eligible residents who are not already receiving social-security pensions. The application and verification dates are scheduled steps; the announcement does not mean applications have already been approved or pensions sanctioned.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Social security and welfare delivery; last-mile public administration; e-governance and beneficiary verification.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Applications are scheduled for 7–16 September through Swarna Gramam and Swarna Ward centres; verification follows in later stages.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how accessible application centres, e-KYC and time-bound verification can improve inclusion while reducing errors in social-protection delivery.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: applications are to be submitted at the State’s Swarna Gramam and Swarna Ward centres.

national.headline: Centre announces three-year roadmap for a drug-free India by 2029
facts: The Union Home Minister announced a three-year roadmap running from July 2026 to July 2029.
The stated goal is a drug-free India by 2029.
The four pillars are intelligence- and operations-based enforcement; control of precursor and synthetic drugs; demand reduction and harm reduction; and capacity-building and coordination.
The government reported more than 11.9 million kg of drugs seized during 2014–2026, compared with 2.6 million kg during 2004–2014.
The release reported 250 million people reached under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan and 570,000 people receiving treatment and rehabilitation.
No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The Union Home Minister announced the roadmap at a narcotics-control press conference in Panaji on 6 September. Its stated pillars combine enforcement and supply control with prevention, treatment and institutional coordination; the 2029 goal is a target, not a completed outcome.
national.staticLink: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985; public-health and harm-reduction approaches; Centre–State coordination.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the roadmap period (July 2026–July 2029), its four pillars and the target year 2029.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how a public-health approach, financial investigation, enforcement and inter-agency coordination can complement each other in tackling drug abuse and trafficking.

national.headline: Sixth RISE Conclave focuses on taking indigenous research from lab to market
facts: The 6th RISE Conclave 2026 opened in Kolkata for a two-day programme on 6–7 September.
The theme was “Driving Innovation & Entrepreneurship for Viksit Bharat 2047”; the event was organised by four CSIR laboratories.
The PIB release reported eight MoUs, four technology transfers, two product launches and one facility inauguration at the conclave.
The programme brought together science, startups, industry and government around technology transfer and commercialisation.
The release cited a ministerial estimate that more than 50–60% of Indian startups are outside metropolitan areas.
No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The conclave highlighted collaboration between public research institutions, startups and industry to commercialise indigenous technologies. Its reported MoUs and technology transfers are event outcomes, not evidence that every technology has already reached commercial scale.

national.headline: National workshop in Panchkula renews focus on vulture conservation and safe landscapes
facts: The Union Environment Minister inaugurated a national vulture-conservation workshop in Panchkula, Haryana, on 6 September.
The workshop theme was “From Crisis to Recovery – Conserving India’s Vultures.”
The Ministry called for continued creation of Vulture Safe Zones, vulture-safe veterinary practices and technical capacity-building.
At Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre, Pinjore, 356 vultures were housed and 35 chicks bred during 2025–26.
The centre released or contributed 87 vultures for reintroduction during 2025–26.
No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The workshop brought together government, scientific and conservation organisations to discuss recovery of India’s vulture populations. The reported breeding and reintroduction figures relate specifically to the Pinjore centre and 2025–26, not to a nationwide population count.
national.staticLink: Vultures as scavengers and ecosystem services; ex-situ conservation; protected landscapes and veterinary drug impacts on wildlife.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Pinjore’s Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre reported 356 vultures housed, 35 chicks bred and 87 birds released or contributed for reintroduction in 2025–26.
national.mainsAngle: Explain how veterinary drug regulation, safe food availability, conservation breeding and community participation can support vulture recovery and ecosystem health.

national.headline: Commerce Minister calls for resilient pharma supply chains and greater R&D at Bharat Health Global Expo
facts: At Bharat Health Global Expo 2026 in New Delhi, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal called for resilient, globally integrated healthcare supply chains.
He urged the pharmaceutical sector to expand beyond generics through research and development, new molecules, biosimilars and biotechnology.
The minister advocated diversified sources of supply and an outward-looking approach, including overseas investment for local value addition and last-mile delivery.
Andhra Pradesh is one of three states with a Union-approved bulk drug park; the approved park is at Nakkapalli in Anakapalli district.
No new investment amount, production capacity or job figure was announced for the Andhra Pradesh park in this expo release.
national.summary: The minister’s remarks framed pharmaceutical supply-chain resilience as a combination of domestic capability, diversified sourcing and global engagement. Andhra Pradesh’s approved bulk drug park at Nakkapalli provides a direct state link to the bulk-drug infrastructure theme, but the expo release did not announce a new project milestone there.
national.staticLink: Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients and Key Starting Materials; industrial clusters; supply-chain resilience; research and innovation policy.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The minister called for pharma R&D in new molecules, biosimilars and biotechnology; AP’s approved bulk drug park is at Nakkapalli, Anakapalli.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how domestic API capacity, R&D investment, diversified imports and common infrastructure can jointly strengthen pharmaceutical security without relying on inward-looking autarky.

national.headline: Defence Minister’s Sri Lanka visit announced for 8–10 September
facts: The Ministry of Defence announced on 6 September that Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh would visit Sri Lanka from 8 to 10 September 2026.
The planned programme included consultations with Sri Lankan leadership and an interaction with the Indian diaspora in Colombo.
A high-level delegation was to include officials from the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of External Affairs.
The PIB framed the visit in the context of India’s Neighbourhood First policy and MAHASAGAR vision.
As of the announcement date, the visit was forthcoming; this item does not treat it as completed.
No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The Ministry of Defence announced a forthcoming visit intended to advance consultations and maritime and defence cooperation with Sri Lanka. The 8–10 September dates were scheduled dates at the time of the announcement, not a report that the visit had already concluded.

international.headline: India and China held senior military commander-level flag talks at Wacha
facts: India and China held a Senior Highest Military Commander-Level Flag Meeting at Wacha in Arunachal Pradesh on 6 September; a corresponding meeting at Damai on the Chinese side followed on 7 September.

The Ministry of External Affairs said the meetings followed understandings between the countries’ Special Representatives and subsequent discussions through the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC).
The engagement concerned military communication and border management along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
international.summary: India and China conducted commander-level flag talks at Wacha on 6 September, followed by a corresponding meeting at Damai on 7 September. international.headline: Seven OPEC+ countries maintained their October oil-production requirements
facts: Seven OPEC+ countries—Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman—met virtually on 6 September 2026.
They decided to maintain their September 2026 required production levels for October 2026 and reaffirmed commitment to the Declaration of Cooperation.
The countries said they would continue monthly reviews; their next meeting was scheduled for 4 October 2026.
India’s exposure to international crude-supply and price conditions makes producer-group decisions relevant to energy security and the external sector.
international.summary: The seven participating OPEC+ countries kept their October production requirements at the September levels after reviewing market conditions. This was a producer-group decision, not a report of observed production or a guarantee of oil prices.
international.staticLink: OPEC+ and producer coordination; energy security; India’s dependence on imported crude oil.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The seven participating countries were Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman; the October requirement stayed at September’s level.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how decisions by major oil producers can affect India’s import bill, inflation risks and energy-security planning.

international.headline: World One Health Congress continued in Lisbon with a focus on science and policy
facts: The 9th World One Health Congress was scheduled in Lisbon, Portugal, from 4 to 7 September 2026; it was underway on 6 September.
WHO, FAO, UNEP and the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) were participating as the Quadripartite partners.
The congress programme covered One Health science and policy, antimicrobial resistance and the science-policy interface.
One Health links human, animal, plant and ecosystem health through cross-sectoral action.
international.summary: The ninth World One Health Congress was in progress in Lisbon on 6 September, bringing together international health and related organisations with researchers and policymakers. Its programme addressed shared human, animal and environmental health challenges; this item records the ongoing meeting, not a new agreement or final outcome.

international.headline: UN–Republic of Korea space-weather workshop announced for Seoul
facts: A report published on 6 September said the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) had announced a UN-cohosted International Space Weather Initiative workshop in Seoul for 7–11 September 2026.
The announced theme was international cooperation and capacity-building in space weather using artificial intelligence.
KASA’s official release dated 7 September confirmed the planned event and described participation by more than 200 experts from around 25 countries.
The workshop was intended to address solar-activity risks to infrastructure including satellites, aviation, navigation, power systems and communications.
international.summary: KASA and the United Nations were set to convene a space-weather workshop in Seoul from 7 September, with AI-based prediction and international capacity-building on the agenda. The announcement concerned a scheduled event; it should not be treated as a completed workshop on 6 September.

international.headline: BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir inaugurated in Paris
